evals.prompt: I'm moving out at the end of next month and want to sell everything I can. I've got Gmail and an Outlook account connected. Go through both and find everything I've bought in the last 5 years that's worth selling.
evals.expected_output: An exhaustive first-pass inventory across both mailboxes, built sender by sender, with ownership checks and a selection sheet the person can mark up.
expectations: Agrees scope before or while starting: time window, exclusions (consumables, items in another country), and whose items count
Confirms which account each mail connector is actually reading
Enumerates order emails by sender with pagination, not only product-keyword searches
Checks more than one Amazon marketplace domain (for example .co.uk, .de, .com, .in)
Covers non-electronics categories such as furniture, homeware, sports kit and bags
Flags returned, refunded or cancelled orders instead of listing them as owned
Produces a selection sheet with a blank SELL? column
Reports coverage (mailbox, sender, date range, pages read) so gaps are visible
Does not describe an unchecked search as 'nothing found'

evals.prompt: What should I list my 249 g camera drone for on eBay? It's about three years old, flown most weekends, and comes with three batteries, the controller and a carry bag.
evals.expected_output: An ask price and a floor backed by sold-price evidence, capped by the current new price, with the legal note on drone registration.
expectations: Bases the price on recent sold prices (eBay's in-form recommended price or sold listings), not asking prices alone
Checks the current new price as a ceiling
Gives both an ask price and a floor
Prices for the actual kit (three batteries, controller, bag) and its heavier use
States the UK rule that a Flyer ID is needed from 100 g (from 1 Jan 2026) and tells the agent or person to re-check current rules
Does not claim a sub-250 g drone needs no registration

evals.prompt: I'm logged in to eBay and Vinted in Chrome. The photos are in ~/Downloads/sale. Make listings for the coffee grinder and the running jacket.
evals.expected_output: Drafts saved in the person's signed-in Chrome, with cleaned photos and nothing published.
expectations: Uses Claude in Chrome, where the person is signed in, not an unsigned built-in browser pane
Strips photo metadata and blurs serials or personal details before upload
Writes a copy-paste listing pack before driving the browser
Saves drafts only and does not publish without an explicit yes for that action
Sets the eBay item location to an area, not the full home postcode
Verifies form fields by reading their values, not only from a screenshot

evals.prompt: Two Vinted buyers, two parcels, and I think I swapped the contents. Both were dropped at a parcel locker an hour ago. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: An immediate, ordered plan that tries to stop the parcel, protects the order and goes through Vinted's support route.
expectations: First tries to stop or retrieve the parcels before the courier collection
Advises messaging the buyer not to confirm receipt
Gives the Vinted support route for the order
Does not claim the existing shipping label can be reused for the correct item
Offers a ready-to-send buyer message

evals.prompt: Make a page I can share with colleagues showing what I'm selling, plus a short post for our workplace sale group. Prices are in my sheet.
evals.expected_output: A buyer-facing page and post that match the sheet, keep the person's colleague prices, and carry item facts only.
expectations: Uses the sheet as the source of truth and keeps its prices
Does not raise colleague prices to match public-market prices without asking
Leaves personal context off the page (moving plans, destination, addresses, prices paid, order numbers)
Shows reserved and sold items as such
Lists items in the post rather than only giving a count

evals.prompt: I've sold a desk lamp, a pair of football boots and a coffee grinder. What box sizes should I buy, and which ones go as a small parcel?
evals.expected_output: A per-item box plan from real product dimensions plus padding, checked against the carrier size and weight bands.
expectations: Looks up or asks for each item's real dimensions and weight
Adds padding allowance and checks fit (for example with scripts/parcel_fit.py)
Maps each parcel to a carrier size and weight band
Tells the person to re-check current carrier limits
